newsitem.title: THAILAND: Ranariddh envoy says conflict past negotiation.
newsitem.headline: Ranariddh envoy says conflict past negotiation.

text.p: The special envoy of Cambodia's first prime minister said on Sunday that the nation's conflict had passed the stage of negotiation and could only be solved through military action.

"In my opinion, the situation in Cambodia has gone past the point of negotiation and it has reached a point where military solution is need to settle the problem," Long Sarin told Reuters in a telephone interview from Surin province near the Cambodian border.

Long Sarin said he had not spoken with First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Sunday, the second day of heavy fighting between forces loyal to Ranariddh and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen in the capital Phnom Penh.
However, he said if the problem could have been solved by talking it would have been resolved before fighting broke out.
Long Sarin acted as the front man for Ranariddh in negotiations with the Khmer Rouge hardliners to end their armed struggle and defect to the government.

Fierce fighting broke out in Phnom Penh on Saturday after Hun Sen said his forces had taken action against defectors from the Khmer Rouge smuggled into the capital by Ranariddh, a charge the prince denied.
King Norodom Sihanouk and several other governments, including Japan, on Sunday called on Ranariddh and Hun Sen to end the fighting in Cambodia and hold talks to settle the problem.
Thousands of people fled the Cambodian capital on Sunday, with at least five killed as forces loyal to the rival prime ministers battled for power.
Long Sarin also told Reuters he was confident that Ranariddh, currently believed to be in Paris visisting family, would return in the near future.

"I am confident that he (Ranariddh) will return as soon as possible and if Phnom Penh was not safe for him we can arrange to save a place for him somewhere else in Cambodia," Long Sarin said. He refused to eleborate.
Hundreds of soldiers loyal to Ranariddh's royalist Funcinpec party are deployed in north and western Cambodia, Long Sarin said.
A Thai general who closely monitors the Cambodian situation, told Reuters he thought the chance of Ranariddh returning to Cambodia was very slim.

Ranariddh issued a statement from Paris late on Saturday accusing Hun Sen of staging a coup. A radio station loyal to Hun Sen denied the accusations and said if it were a coup Ranariddh's party officials and supporters would have been arrested.
